banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.name: Mekong Delta Sesbania Flower Bánh Xèo
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.serving_basis: About eight medium crepes, two per person, served with fresh greens and tamarind fish sauce.
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.description: Sesbania flower bánh xèo is associated with the Mekong Delta flood season, when the yellow blossoms are placed in the filling rather than served only as a side green. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with shrimp, pork belly, bean sprouts and seasonal sesbania flowers; a light coconut mixture makes the crepe fragrant while keeping it crisp. Use only flowers sold as food from a safe source, wash them well and drain thoroughly.
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.finished_dish: Thin golden crepes with crisp edges, just-cooked shrimp and pork, bean sprouts and intact sesbania flowers; fresh greens and tamarind sauce balance the gentle richness.
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.serving: Serve hot. Break off a piece, wrap it with lettuce and herbs, then dip it in tamarind fish sauce. Do not stack the crepes for long, as trapped steam softens the crust.
tips: Rest the batter for 20 minutes, then stir again; if it is thick, add water a little at a time so it spreads thinly.
Dry the sesbania flowers after washing to reduce oil splatter and keep the crepes crisp.
Cover briefly to cook the filling, then uncover and keep the heat moderate until the edges dry and crisp.
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.image_alt: Golden Mekong Delta bánh xèo with shrimp, pork, bean sprouts and sesbania flowers on a ceramic plate; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-xeo-bong-dien-dien.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including 20 minutes for the batter to rest; frying time varies with pan size.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift to remove lumps.

ingredients.name: Light coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Dilute thick coconut milk with water if needed.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust until the batter is thin enough to spread.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel and devein.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Sesbania flowers
ingredients.notes: Use flowers from a safe food source; remove tough stems, wash and drain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain.

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: For a gentle golden color.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Finely sliced.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the batter.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use a little for each crepe.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water and strain.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the tartness of the tamarind.

preparation_steps: Whisk the rice flour with light coconut milk, water, turmeric and salt until smooth. Stir in the scallions, rest for 20 minutes, then stir once more.
Peel and devein the shrimp; thinly slice the pork belly. Gently pick over and wash the sesbania flowers, then drain thoroughly; wash the bean sprouts and fresh herbs.
Soak the tamarind in about 60 ml warm water and strain. Mix the extract with fish sauce, sugar and 60 ml warm water; taste and add garlic and chili if desired.
cooking_steps: Heat a 20–22 cm nonstick pan and lightly coat it with oil. Add a few slices of pork and shrimp; cook until the shrimp just changes color.
Pour in a ladle of batter and tilt the pan to make a thin layer. Add a small amount of bean sprouts and sesbania flowers to one half.
Cover for 2–3 minutes until the filling cooks. Uncover, reduce to medium heat and fry another 2–4 minutes until the edge is crisp, then fold the crepe in half.
Transfer the crepe to a plate lined with paper towel. Repeat with the remaining ingredients, keeping the finished crepes in a single layer so they do not steam-soften.

com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.name: Northwest Vietnam Bamboo-Tube Sticky Rice
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.serving_basis: Four small bamboo tubes, one per person; serve with sesame salt or grilled dishes.
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.description: Cơm lam is a way of cooking glutinous rice in bamboo or reed tubes over a fire and is recorded across several Northwest provinces. Bếp Việt edits a home batch with overnight-soaked upland sticky rice, a little salt and ginger; the rice cooks tender and fragrant inside the young bamboo membrane. Families and local areas differ in seasoning, tube choice and accompaniments.
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.finished_dish: Evenly cooked sticky rice in bamboo tubes, glossy and tender with a light roasted-bamboo aroma; serve with nutty sesame salt.
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.serving: Let the tubes cool slightly, peel away the outer bamboo and keep the thin inner membrane attached to the rice. Cut into serving pieces and eat with sesame salt; grilled stream fish or pork can be served alongside.
tips: Soak and drain the rice well so it cooks evenly without a hard center.
Fill the tubes only about two-thirds full and leave room for the rice to expand.
Turn the tubes regularly over glowing coals; one side can char before the rice cooks if left facing the heat.
search_terms: what to serve with cơm lam
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.image_alt: Four roasted Northwest sticky-rice bamboo tubes on a ceramic platter, one split to show glossy rice with a bowl of sesame salt; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
com-lam-nep-nuong-tay-bac.time_note: About 9 hours 10 minutes, including overnight rice soaking; grilling time varies with tube size and coal heat.

ingredients.name: Upland glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Pick through and rinse gently to avoid breaking the grains.

ingredients.name: Young bamboo tubes
ingredients.notes: Fresh, clean tubes about 25–30 cm long; leave one bamboo node at the bottom.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For soaking and moistening the rice; add only enough to barely cover the rice in each tube.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Mix into the rice before filling the tubes.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Cut into fine strips; optional to taste.

ingredients.name: White sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Toast for the sesame-salt accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush coarsely and mix with the sesame and a little salt.

preparation_steps: Rinse the rice gently and soak it in clean water for 6–8 hours or overnight. Rinse once more, drain and mix with salt and finely sliced ginger.
Clean the inside of the bamboo tubes and let them drain. Divide the rice among four tubes, filling only about two-thirds; add water just to the top of the rice.
Plug the openings with clean banana leaf or young bamboo leaf. Prepare a steady bed of glowing coals without large flames.
cooking_steps: Set the tubes on a rack above the coals. Turn each tube regularly so the bamboo heats evenly and does not burn on one side.
Grill for about 40–50 minutes, depending on tube thickness. The rice is ready when it smells cooked, the bamboo contracts and a test grain is tender throughout.
Remove the tubes and rest for 5 minutes. Peel the outer bamboo while warm, keeping the thin membrane on the rice. Toast the sesame, crush the peanuts and mix them into sesame salt.

banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.name: Vũng Tàu Crab Bánh Canh
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.serving_basis: Four medium bowls, each with one portion of crab and thick noodles.
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.description: Bánh canh ghẹ is a familiar seafood noodle soup in Vũng Tàu; its broth is commonly simmered with crab and pork bones for a rounded natural sweetness. Bếp Việt edits a home version with thick bánh canh noodles, blue swimmer crab, shallot and a little annatto oil for a warm, clear broth.
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.finished_dish: A hot bowl of thick, pleasantly chewy noodles with sweet crab meat and a clean, seafood-forward broth topped with a little scallion and cilantro.
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.serving: Place the noodles in bowls and ladle over boiling broth. Add the crab meat, claws, scallion and cilantro. Serve hot with pepper, lime and chili to taste.
tips: Choose fresh crabs with intact shells; steaming them separately keeps the meat from breaking down in the broth.
Skim the pork-bone broth as it simmers for a clearer, cleaner flavor.
Blanch the noodles separately if they have excess surface starch, so the soup does not become too thick.
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.image_alt: A bowl of Vũng Tàu bánh canh with thick noodles, crab meat and claws in a light golden broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-canh-ghe-vung-tau.time_note: About 1 hour 15 minutes for prep, broth and crab; fresh noodles shorten the cooking time.

ingredients.name: Blue swimmer crab
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh crabs, scrub clean and divide between steaming and broth.

ingredients.name: Pork bones
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly and rinse before simmering.

ingredients.name: Thick bánh canh noodles
ingredients.notes: Fresh or packaged noodles; follow package directions.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush; some will be fried until fragrant.

ingredients.name: Scallion and cilantro
ingredients.notes: Wash and chop.

ingredients.name: Annatto oil
ingredients.notes: Optional; adds a light color.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season near the end, adjusting to the broth's saltiness.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the broth.

ingredients.name: Rock sugar
ingredients.notes: Adds a gentle finish.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add when serving.

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse. Scrub the crabs clean, remove the apron and gills, and drain.
Peel and crush the shallots. Wash and chop the scallions and cilantro. If the noodles have a heavy coating of starch, rinse briefly and drain.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones in 1.8 liters of water. Bring to a boil, skim, then cook gently for 35 minutes; strain the broth if needed.
Steam the crabs for 8–10 minutes, until the shells turn red-orange and the meat is just cooked. Cool slightly, pick the meat and keep a few claws whole for serving.
Fry the shallots in annatto oil, add the crab meat and gently stir for 1 minute. Add it to the broth and season with fish sauce, salt and rock sugar.
Blanch the noodles following the package directions and divide among four bowls. Pour over the boiling broth, add crab meat and claws, scallion, cilantro and pepper.

bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.name: Krông Pa One-Sun Beef with Ant-Egg Salt
aliases: One-sun beef with muối kiến vàng
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.serving_basis: One 500 g plate of prepared beef to share with vegetables and rice paper for 3–4 people.
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.description: One-sun beef served with muối kiến vàng is a regional pairing associated with Krông Pa, Gia Lai and Central Highlands food culture. The beef is seasoned and dried in the sun for a day before it is cooked for serving; this Bếp Việt home version uses commercially prepared, labeled one-sun beef, quickly grilled and served with food-grade ant-egg salt.
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.finished_dish: Warm one-sun beef with lightly charred edges and tender slices inside; muối kiến vàng adds savory, tangy, spicy and aromatic notes.
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.serving: Rest the beef for 3 minutes, then slice across the grain. Serve with muối kiến vàng, herbs or rice paper, following the package's storage and cooking instructions.
tips: Choose labeled one-sun beef with a clear use-by date and storage directions; thaw in the refrigerator if frozen.
Preheat the grill and cook briefly on each side; prolonged grilling makes the meat dry and tough.
Muối kiến vàng may contain insect allergens; check ingredients and avoid it if you have a related allergy.
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.image_alt: Grilled and sliced Gia Lai one-sun beef on a ceramic plate with a bowl of muối kiến vàng and a lime wedge; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bo-mot-nang-muoi-kien-vang-krong-pa.time_note: About 22 minutes using prepared one-sun beef; the traditional seasoning and sun-drying time is not part of this reheating recipe.

ingredients.name: Prepared one-sun beef
ingredients.notes: Choose a labeled product and store it as directed; thaw in the refrigerator if needed.

ingredients.name: Food-grade muối kiến vàng
ingredients.notes: Use a packaged product with a clear source; check for allergens.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges and serve to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain well.

ingredients.name: Rice paper
ingredients.notes: For wrapping, if desired.

preparation_steps: Check the label, use-by date and storage condition of the one-sun beef and ant-egg salt. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator and pat the surface dry.
Wash and drain the herbs; cut the lime into wedges. Preheat a grill or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
cooking_steps: Lightly oil the grill if needed. Grill the beef for about 2–3 minutes per side, turning once, until heated through and lightly charred; follow the producer's directions.
Remove the beef, rest for 3 minutes and slice thinly across the grain. Arrange with muối kiến vàng, herbs, lime and rice paper.

chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.name: Quảng Bình Cháo Canh with Snakehead Fish
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.serving_basis: Four medium bowls, each with thick dough noodles, snakehead fish and mustard greens.
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.description: Cháo canh is a rustic specialty of Quảng Bình. Despite the word cháo, the dish is a noodle soup made with thick wheat- or rice-flour noodles, snakehead fish, meat and mustard greens. Bếp Việt edits a fish version with pork-bone stock, củ nén and turmeric; fresh noodles are used to simplify the home preparation.
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.finished_dish: Thick, tender noodles in a hot broth with lightly turmeric-colored snakehead fish and just-cooked mustard greens; the broth is gently thickened, not like rice porridge.
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.serving: Serve while piping hot with scallion and black pepper. Crispy ram rolls can accompany the bowl as they do in local servings; add chili if desired.
tips: Choose fresh or packaged cháo canh noodles and follow the package cooking time so they do not break down.
Cook the fish just until done, remove all bones carefully and strain the poaching liquid for a clean broth.
Add the mustard greens at the end; once the broth returns to a boil, turn off the heat to keep the greens bright and crisp.
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.image_alt: A bowl of Quảng Bình cháo canh with thick noodles, turmeric snakehead fish, mustard greens and scallion in broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
chao-canh-ca-loc-quang-binh.time_note: About 1 hour 5 minutes with fresh noodles; cooking time varies with the noodle type.

ingredients.name: Snakehead fish
ingredients.notes: Clean and cut into pieces; filleted fish can be used, reserving bones for stock.

ingredients.name: Pork bones
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly and rinse clean.

ingredients.name: Fresh cháo canh noodles
ingredients.notes: Choose thick wheat- or rice-flour noodles; for dried noodles, follow the package directions.

ingredients.name: Mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Wash and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Củ nén
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush; shallot can be used if unavailable.

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: Season the fish for a light golden color.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the fish and broth in two additions.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the củ nén and fish.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle at the end.

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones for 3 minutes in boiling water and rinse. Clean and cut the fish; season it with half the fish sauce, turmeric and a little salt for 10 minutes.
Wash and cut the mustard greens. Peel and crush the củ nén; wash and slice the scallions. Prepare the noodles according to the package directions.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones in 1.5 liters of water for 30 minutes, skimming regularly. Poach the fish separately until just cooked, lift it out to remove the bones and strain the poaching liquid into the stock.
Fry the củ nén in oil until fragrant. Add the picked fish and gently turn for 1–2 minutes with the remaining fish sauce, keeping the pieces intact.
Season the broth with salt, pepper and fish sauce. Add the cháo canh noodles and cook according to the package timing until tender and slightly chewy, and the broth is lightly thickened.
Return the fish to the pot, add the mustard greens and bring back to a boil for about 1 minute. Turn off the heat, ladle into bowls and top with scallions and pepper.
